summary:
**LUNARIS – Interactive Lunar Exploration and Mission Planning Platform**

LUNARIS is an interactive web-based platform developed to make lunar exploration more accessible through 3D visualization, mission simulations and location-based analysis. It features separate 3D Earth and Moon explorers, an individual satellite database, and a Mission Lab offering different mission scenarios, including thermal mapping, surface analysis and satellite deployment.

Users can select custom lunar latitude and longitude coordinates, investigate potential landing locations and receive indicative landing-compatibility assessments. Additional tools such as Earth Visibility Analysis, Horizon Analysis and Site Comparison introduce important factors involved in lunar mission planning.

Developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, LUNARIS combines interactive exploration with preliminary computational assessments. It addresses the challenge by allowing users to visualize, investigate and better understand the complexities of lunar exploration rather than simply reading about them. Its purpose is to encourage scientific curiosity and demonstrate how interactive technology can support space science education and preliminary mission investigation.
details:
Project Details – LUNARIS

LUNARIS is a project I independently conceptualized and developed with the goal of making lunar exploration more interactive, accessible and understandable. Rather than creating another website that simply provides information about space, I wanted to build something that allows users to actively explore the Moon, investigate potential landing locations and experiment with different mission scenarios.

The platform combines several features into one environment. It includes separate interactive 3D Earth and Moon explorers, a satellite database containing individual satellite profiles, and a Mission Lab with different exploration scenarios such as thermal mapping, surface analysis and satellite deployment concepts.

One of the features I particularly focused on was custom lunar coordinate selection. Instead of limiting users to predefined locations, I wanted them to be able to enter their own latitude and longitude and investigate potential landing regions. LUNARIS provides indicative landing-compatibility assessments based on the selected locations. It also incorporates Earth Visibility Analysis, Horizon Analysis and Site Comparison to introduce users to important considerations involved in lunar mission planning.

My approach to developing LUNARIS was also important to me. I independently came up with the concept, planned the platform, designed its interface, developed its features and worked through the technical challenges involved in bringing everything together. I used HTML, CSS and JavaScript to build the application and Netlify to deploy it publicly.

In today's world, where Artificial Intelligence is increasingly capable of generating code and applications, I deliberately wanted to challenge myself by doing the majority of the development independently. I used little to no AI assistance in creating the actual project, prioritizing my own problem-solving, experimentation, coding and learning. I wanted the final result to reflect my own understanding and effort rather than simply relying on an AI-generated application.

The development process involved continuous experimentation, identifying errors, fixing functionality and refining different sections. I particularly focused on making every section serve a distinct purpose rather than creating features that were interactive in appearance but offered little meaningful functionality.

The main factors I considered were usability, scientific relevance, accessibility, visual clarity and the distinction between simulated assessments and scientifically verified mission data. I wanted LUNARIS to be visually engaging while still introducing meaningful concepts related to lunar exploration.

The intended impact of LUNARIS is to encourage curiosity about space exploration and make complex lunar mission concepts easier to understand. It could serve as an educational platform for students, space enthusiasts and anyone interested in understanding the challenges of exploring the Moon.

I see LUNARIS as more than a website. It represents my interest in space technology, my willingness to learn independently and my belief that meaningful projects can be created through curiosity, persistence and experimentation.

My vision is to make space exploration something people do not just read about, but something they can actively explore and understand.
